questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has ABS, what can you do?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface and feel if ABS activates.
Assume the trailer has ABS.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). A yellow warning light shows if ABS is working. For older trailers, check underneath for wires and sensors connected to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes must be:

options.text: Disengaged.
Locked.
Deactivated.
Dry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locked.
questions.explanation: When coupling trailers, always lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under it. This is a key safety step for operating combination vehicles.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, the landing gear should be:

options.text: Raised completely.
Lowered halfway.
Just slightly touching the ground.
Resting firmly on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Resting firmly on the ground.
questions.explanation: Always raise landing gear completely before driving. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it touches the ground firmly. For loaded trailers, turn the crank a few extra times to remove weight from the trailer.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: A square blue knob.
A triangular yellow knob.
An eight-sided red knob.
A circular orange knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: An eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob on newer vehicles. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on downhill slopes.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. Using it can cause all air to leak out of the brakes, causing them to release. Instead, use the parking brake.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, you should:

options.text: Move cargo to the left side of the truck.
Keep cargo centered on the truck.
Move cargo to the right side of the truck.
Keep cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo centered on the truck.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading increases rollover risk. Keep loads centered on the truck to prevent dangerous rollovers.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need more road space than other trucks because they are longer and:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.
Drive more slowly.
Are twice as wide.
Swerve more often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and require more space to turn and stop. Space management is critical when driving these vehicles.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
Only the rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open except the rear ones.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open except the rear ones.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones at the rear of the trailer. This ensures air reaches all brakes while preventing air from escaping at the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: A trailer is most likely to swing out when it is:

options.text: Full.
Traveling in a straight line.
Empty.
The wheels are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Empty.
questions.explanation: Empty trailers need longer stopping distances than loaded ones. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails stop very easily.
Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without a trailer attached. Bobtails are difficult to stop and need a longer distance to stop than a tractor pulling a loaded trailer.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
It prevents the truck from being stolen.
It prevents the driver from going too fast.
It prevents the trailer from accidentally disconnecting.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck's brake system. This is important if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer straight, what should you do?

options.text: Back toward the passenger's side.
Back toward the driver's side.
Swerve back and forth while backing.
Always turn to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back toward the driver's side.
questions.explanation: Back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a jackknife?

options.text: It stops the skid.
It straightens the trailer.
It improves traction.
It continues the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: It continues the skid.
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand brake during a skid makes it worse. Release the brakes to help your tires regain traction.

questions.question: How does a fully-loaded truck compare to an empty truck for rollover risk?

options.text: It is less likely to roll over.
It is more likely to roll over.
It has the same chance of rolling over.
It should not be driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded trucks have a higher center of gravity. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty trucks.

questions.question: How should you load cargo to reduce rollover risk?

options.text: Load it as far forward as possible.
Load it as far back as possible.
Load it as low as possible.
Stack it as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly to reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Back up slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
Back up slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
questions.explanation: First check that the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and use the hand control to apply the brakes. You should feel the brakes activate.

questions.question: What is one function of the emergency air line?

options.text: Control the emergency brakes.
Flash when air pressure is low.
Allow for quick turning.
Control steering in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Control the emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: What is the easiest way to notice your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Ask another driver.
Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left the lane.
Release and press the brake pedal again.
Watch for a jackknife warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left the lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. Check them anytime you brake hard to make sure the trailer is in the correct position.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle turns a corner?

options.text: The turn should be made as tightly as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is acceptable to knock over street signs if they are too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. It is more pronounced on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: How should you brake in a tractor-trailer with ABS?

options.text: Brake harder than normal.
Use extra force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way you normally would.
Brake with less pressure than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you normally would.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
